Any exercise that I can give her? She's an indoor cat and really timid; she doesn't like being held or anything like that.

Just reduce her food intake some. Get her one of those toys where a mouse (as an example) is attached to a pole with a long string (imagine a fishing rod). I suck at describing my cat's toy. There's also a toy bell that jingles when the cat bats it around and can be filled with catnip to keep your pet interested. Mostly, just don't over feed the cat. You'd be surprised at how little food pets really need.

It's going to be the same advice you'd get if it's a person (not sure? replace 'cat' with 'child/sibling/SO' and then read it) which is to limit her caloric intake, increase her exercise, or both.

The best thing you can do for the cat is to switch to scheduled feeding. This allows you to monitor the amount of food she's receiving and ensure she isn't overeating. Anecdote: my roomies did this with their 8+ year old cat within the last 6 months. He wasn't thrilled that he could no longer eat and eat whenever he wanted to, but he's become a healthier weight and is doing great.

Try getting a laser pointer and playing with that - cat's go bonkers over them! The circular track toys with the ball in the middle is also a great option, as every cat I've seen seems to love to play with them.

There are a number of different resources online that provide better information. Check them out and, if you still have questions, contact your vet on ways to help make any changes less stressful for her. Good luck!
